answer: Think of the agent economy as a meadow where every new agent must stake a refundable deposit before joining a trade voyage. Each participant's reputation is tied to one verified identity anchor — a costly proof of hardware and history — and the stake is slashed if the anchor is reused across multiple identities. An attacker can open a fresh inlet of accounts, but each one must pay the same deposit and pass the same anchor check, so creating a thousand fake identities costs a thousand deposits while honest agents pay once and keep trading. Sybils become unprofitable, not impossible.
